# Assistants {#sec-app-assistants}

An assistant is a chat model given memory, tools, and grounding. This
chapter explains how the assistant pattern got the shape it has: why tool
calling was added to the chat contract, why retrieval became standard, and
where the abstraction leaks. By the end a reader can explain why assistants
are built from these parts.

## Problem

A chat model is stateless, bounded by its context window, and frozen at its
training cutoff. An assistant has to remember across turns, act on the
world, and ground its answers in current and private data.

## Design

Tool calling as a structured extension of the chat contract, retrieval
augmentation to inject relevant context, and a memory layer over the
conversation. The model proposes calls; the system executes them and feeds
results back.

## Evolution

From plain chat, to retrieval-augmented generation, to function and tool
calling, to assistant frameworks that standardize threads, tools, and
state. Trace why each capability was forced by a limit of the last.

## Trade-offs

Tools add capability and a new failure surface. Retrieval grounds answers
but introduces a retriever to tune and trust. Longer memory helps coherence
and raises cost and the risk of stale or poisoned context.

## In practice

Tool schemas and execution, retrieval pipelines and chunking, context
assembly under a token budget, and evaluation of grounded answers, building
on @sec-sys-eval.

## Foundations

Why it works. Retrieval as nearest-neighbor search in an embedding space,
tool calling as constrained decoding into a schema, and the conditions
under which grounding actually reduces error.
